questions.question: How can alcohol affect you while driving?

options.text: It makes you feel overly confident.
It reduces your ability to think clearly.

questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. You may feel confident or silly. Alcohol also slows your reaction time, hurts your coordination, and affects your balance. Your vision and ability to judge distance get worse, making it hard to respond to what's around you.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your hazard flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your hazard flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: If your car breaks down on the highway, turn on your hazard flashers. Move as far off the road as possible. Lift your hood so other drivers know your car is disabled.

questions.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is likely to be:
questions.explanation: You must always give the right-of-way to a pedestrian who is blind and using a white cane or guide dog.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks are allowed on the bridge ahead.
The bridge ahead is one-way only.
Only one car can fit on the bridge at a time.
The bridge ahead may be too narrow to pass a truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bridge ahead may be too narrow to pass a truck.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to hazards ahead. They are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the bridge may be too narrow to pass a truck. Be careful.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light, you should:
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard ahead. Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs prepare you for road hazards. They are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you a T intersection is coming. Be ready to turn left or right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means an intersection is coming. Watch for traffic crossing your path.

questions.question: Alcohol causes:
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol hurts your vision, judgment, focus, and coordination.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate highway, what should you do?

options.text: Get off at the next exit and go back to your missed exit.
Ask the driver next to you for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and go back to your missed exit.
questions.explanation: Do not back up or turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: Road rage and aggressive driving can be reduced by:
questions.explanation: To help prevent road rage, use turn signals, follow speed limits, and allow plenty of time to reach your destination.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Turn your head quickly to check for other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check both mirrors for traffic behind you. Just before you move, turn your head quickly to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Wait for your body to process the alcohol naturally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to process the alcohol naturally.
questions.explanation: Only time can lower your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot reduce your BAC or make you sober. They may help you stay awake, but they do not change your BAC.

questions.question: Which of these commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Driving too fast for road conditions

questions.explanation: Driving too fast causes many crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Most rear-end collisions happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: A driver who goes much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Should not let cars behind pass.

questions.explanation: Driving much slower than traffic can be unsafe. On a two-lane road, you must pull over to let cars pass if traffic backs up behind you. Only drive slowly when road conditions require it.

questions.question: A seat belt should be adjusted so that it:

options.text: Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Stops the belt alarm from going off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should be comfortable with enough room to fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?

options.text: When pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder every time you change your vehicle's position. This includes turning, changing lanes, and pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: If in an accident, a driver should:

options.text: Stop their vehicle at or near the scene.
Turn off the ignitions of damaged vehicles.

questions.explanation: After an accident, stop at or near the scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if possible. Do not stand in traffic lanes where another vehicle could hit you. Turn off the ignitions of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: Worn or bald tires:

options.text: Are more likely to skid on wet roads.

questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase stopping distance and make turning harder. They also increase the risk of skidding on wet roads.

questions.question: When getting ready to turn left, drivers should:

options.text: Slow down gradually and check the rearview mirror.
Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.explanation: Signal your left turn three to five seconds early. Check your rearview mirror as you slow down gradually. Move into the left lane before you reach the intersection. Yield to traffic and pedestrians, then turn when it is safe.

questions.question: To stay out of a truck or bus driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Do not drive next to them and do not tailgate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive next to them and do not tailgate.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles like trucks and buses have big blind spots on the sides and rear. Avoid driving next to them and do not follow too closely.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing red or blue lights?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up.
Keep driving but stay out of its way.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must let all emergency vehicles pass. Pull over to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep hill is coming.

questions.question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, you should:

options.text: Get out of the aggressive driver's way.
Stare at the driver as they pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: Move out of the way of an aggressive driver. Do not make eye contact. Do not speed up, as this may make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: When it starts to sleet or snow, you should:

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Leave more distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: In snow, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Increase the distance between you and other vehicles because icy roads make it harder to stop.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. You should:

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Always stop for pedestrians. Slow down and be ready to stop whenever you see someone walking or crossing the road. Be extra careful around children. Give pedestrians in crosswalks the right-of-way.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Look at what other cars are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means red is coming. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: When you are in an accident, you should:

options.text: Not exchange information with other drivers.
Exchange all information with other drivers.
Let the other driver report the accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exchange all information with other drivers.
questions.explanation: Exchange names, addresses, driver license numbers, vehicle details (license plate, make, model, year), and insurance information with the other driver.

questions.question: What can happen when alcohol is mixed with another drug?

options.text: The effects of both may be stronger.
The effects of both may be weaker.
Only the alcohol effect may be weaker.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both may be stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make both effects stronger. For example, one drink combined with a cold medicine can affect you like several drinks.

questions.question: You are driving and hear a siren behind you. You should:

options.text: Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights behind you, pull over to the right side of the road and stop. Slow down and make space for the emergency vehicle. If you are in heavy traffic, move slowly until you can get out of the way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you a winding road is ahead. Slow down and be ready for curves.
